# phase-112 — Make `else if` parse, as SPEC.md and docs/GRAMMAR.md both promise

## You must change `src/ or corpus/ or tests/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [src/ or corpus/ or tests/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
SPEC.md:391 writes `else if x < 0` inside a worked `if/else` example, and docs/GRAMMAR.md:221 writes `{ 'else if' expression 'then' { statement } }` as part of `if_statement`. src/parser.rs:791 `fn parse_if` has no else-if arm: after consuming `TokenKind::Else` at src/parser.rs:812 it enters a plain statement loop, so the `if` is parsed as a NESTED `if`, that nested `if` consumes the `end` that belonged to the outer one, and the outer `parse_if` then fails its `self.expect(__FINDING__TokenKind::End)` at src/parser.rs:830. Verified against the built binary this audit: `else if` is a parse error in EVERY position - as the last branch (`ParserError: Expected 'end' but got Eof` at 7:1), as a middle branch with a trailing `else` (9:1), and two chained `else if`s with a trailing `else` (11:1). corpus/control-flow-0003.rb:3, corpus/control-flow-0004.rb:3 and corpus/control-flow-0005.rb:3 are the only three corpus programs that write `else if`, and all three are recorded as must-fail; tests/differential_test.rs:718-746 pins that refusal on both engines so it cannot change silently. The documentation has promised this form for the whole life of the project and no program can use it.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Parse `else if <expr> then ... ` as a real else-if chain so the form SPEC.md:391 and docs/GRAMMAR.md:221 document actually runs, and move the three corpus programs off the must-fail list deliberately.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-112
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `if x is 9 then say "nine" else if x is 1 then say "one" end` prints `one`, and the same with a trailing `else` prints the right branch
- [ ] two or more chained `else if` arms with a trailing `else` work in both engines, and `rb run` and `rb compile` + `rb vm` agree
- [ ] a plain `if`/`else` with no `else if` is unchanged, pinned by a test
- [ ] an `else if` chain with a missing `then`, a missing `end`, and an `else` with nothing after it each produce a positioned ParserError naming what was expected - never a panic
- [ ] corpus/control-flow-0003.rb, -0004.rb and -0005.rb stop being must-fail, their .expected files are regenerated, and `cargo test --test differential_test` still passes with tests/differential_test.rs:701-746 deliberately updated to assert the chain NOW parses rather than deleted
- [ ] edge_* tests cover: else-if as the last arm, else-if in the middle, three arms, an empty then-branch in an else-if arm, `else if` inside a `for`/`while`/`repeat` body, and a nested `if` inside an `else if` arm
- [ ] docs/GRAMMAR.md and SPEC.md agree with the implementation afterwards
- [ ] `cargo test` reports 0 failures and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean
